from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Lifeguard Problem", [
            "A lifeguard must reach a swimmer quickly.",
            "Running speed on sand exceeds swimming speed.",
            "The path bends to minimize total time."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        sand = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0)
        water = Rectangle(width=6, height=3, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=0)
        boundary = Line(start=[-3, 0, 0], end=[3, 0, 0], color=WHITE)
        
        lifeguard = Dot(color=YELLOW).scale(1.5)
        swimmer = Dot(color=RED).scale(1.5)
        
        # Helper to group objects for placement
        scene_elements = VGroup(sand, water, boundary, lifeguard, swimmer)
        self.place_in_area(scene_elements, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Positioning
        self.place_at_grid(sand, "B3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(water, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(boundary, "C3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(lifeguard, "A3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(swimmer, "F4", scale_factor=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(sand), FadeIn(water), FadeIn(boundary), FadeIn(lifeguard), FadeIn(swimmer))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        sand_label = Text("Faster", font_size=20, color=YELLOW)
        water_label = Text("Slower", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(sand_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(water_label, "E5")
        self.play(Write(sand_label), Write(water_label))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        path = ArcBetweenPoints(lifeguard.get_center(), swimmer.get_center(), angle=-TAU/12, color=GREEN)
        self.play(Create(path))
        self.wait(4)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Derivation", [
            "Express total time as function of distance.",
            "T equals sum of times in media.",
            "Set derivative to zero for minimum time."
        ])
        
        # Colors for highlights
        c1 = "#FF9999"
        c2 = "#99FF99"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # T = (sqrt(y1^2 + x^2))/v1 + (sqrt(y2^2 + (L-x)^2))/v2
        time_eq = MathTex(
            r"T(x) = \frac{\sqrt{y_1^2 + x^2}}{v_1} + \frac{\sqrt{y_2^2 + (L-x)^2}}{v_2}", 
            font_size=32
        )
        self.place_at_grid(time_eq, 'B2')
        self.play(Write(time_eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(c1)
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Differentiate T with respect to x
        dt_dx = MathTex(
            r"\frac{dT}{dx} = \frac{x}{v_1\sqrt{y_1^2 + x^2}} - \frac{L-x}{v_2\sqrt{y_2^2 + (L-x)^2}} = 0",
            font_size=30
        )
        self.place_at_grid(dt_dx, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(dt_dx))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(c2)
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Snell's Law result
        snells = MathTex(
            r"\frac{\sin\theta_1}{v_1} = \frac{\sin\theta_2}{v_2}",
            font_size=40, color=YELLOW
        )
        self.place_at_grid(snells, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(snells))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(4)

outline.topic: The Derivation of Snell’s Law: Fermat’s Principle

sections.title: Hook & Intuition: The Lifeguard Problem
sections.content: Introduce the problem: A lifeguard on the beach sees a swimmer in distress. They must choose the path that takes the minimum time, not necessarily the shortest distance, because they run faster than they swim.
sections.example: Visualize a lifeguard running on sand (fast medium) versus swimming in water (slow medium). The path bends at the boundary to save total time.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle of Least Time
sections.content: Define Fermat’s Principle: Light always follows the path that requires the least time to travel between two points. This is the foundational axiom for deriving the laws of optics.
sections.example: Animation showing light rays as 'intelligent' messengers choosing the fastest route through varying refractive indices.

sections.title: Setting the Geometric Model
sections.content: Set up the coordinate system: Define an interface between medium 1 (n1) and medium 2 (n2). Let light travel from point A to point B, crossing at point x on the boundary. Define angles of incidence (θ1) and refraction (θ2) relative to the normal.
sections.example: A clear diagram showing the boundary, the two media, and variables: x (horizontal distance), y1, y2 (vertical distances), and v1, v2 (velocities).

sections.title: Mathematical Derivation: Minimizing the Time Function
sections.content: Express total time T(x) as the sum of time in medium 1 and 2: T(x) = (sqrt(y1² + x²))/v1 + (sqrt(y2² + (L-x)²))/v2. Use calculus: Set dT/dx = 0 to find the minimum time condition.
sections.example: An animated graph where a point 'x' slides along the interface; as it hits the optimal spot, the 'Time' meter minimizes, revealing the derivative equals zero.

sections.title: Synthesis: Snell’s Law
sections.content: Transform the derivative results into trigonometric ratios (sinθ1/v1 = sinθ2/v2). Substitute v = c/n to arrive at the final form: n1 sinθ1 = n2 sinθ2.
sections.example: Final screen showing the transition from calculus to the iconic elegant formula: n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2).
